\section{Hypercontractivity --- Cube --- One Bit}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Cube.OneBit
\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Cube --- One Bit: Introduction}
Fourier coefficients describe every function on one bit, and scalar two-point inequalities yield sharp one-bit norm bounds. Holder extremizers and self-adjointness provide duality and the complementary high-exponent estimate.

\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Cube --- One Bit: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Enumeration of the one-bit Boolean cube]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.boolCube1_univ}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube}
\difficulty{1}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.boolCube1_univ}
On the one-dimensional Boolean hypercube $\{0,1\}^1$, whose points are the functions
from a single-element index set to $\{0,1\}$, the set of all points consists of exactly
the two constant functions: the one taking the value $0$ (false) and the one taking the
value $1$ (true).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The two subsets of a one-element set]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.finsetFin1_univ}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.finsetFin1_univ}
The power set of the singleton $\{0\}$ is exactly $\{\varnothing,\{0\}\}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The two constant one-bit inputs differ]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.boolCube1_ne}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.boolCube1_ne}
The two functions from the singleton $\{0\}$ to $\{0,1\}$ that are constantly $0$ and
constantly $1$ are distinct.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Empty subset differs from the singleton in $\mathrm{Fin}\,1$]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.finsetFin1_ne}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.finsetFin1_ne}
The empty subset $\varnothing$ and the singleton subset $\{0\}$ of the set $\{0\}$ are
distinct.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Value of a one-bit function at the false input]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_bit_val_false}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.finsetFin1_ne, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.finsetFin1_univ, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.walsh_expansion}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p022-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p023-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p024-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p025-b004
}
\difficulty{3}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_bit_val_false}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^1\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function of arity $1$, and let $x_0\in\{0,1\}^1$
be the input whose single coordinate is $\mathit{false}$ (that is, the sign encoding of
that coordinate is $+1$). Then the value of $f$ at this input equals the sum of its
degree-zero and degree-one Fourier--Walsh coefficients:
\[
  f(x_0) \;=\; \hat f(\emptyset) + \hat f(\{0\}).
\]
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{3}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_bit_val_true}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^1\to\bbr$ be a function of a single bit, and write $\hat
f(\emptyset)$ and $\hat f(\{0\})$ for its two Fourier--Walsh coefficients, where $\{0\}$
is the singleton frequency consisting of the sole coordinate. If $x_1$ is the input
whose single coordinate is $1$ (the bit value corresponding to $-1$ under the sign
encoding), its value is the difference of these two coefficients,
\[
  f(x_1) \;=\; \hat f(\emptyset) - \hat f(\{0\}).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Expected square of a noised one-bit function]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_noiseOp_sq_one_bit}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.finsetFin1_ne, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.finsetFin1_univ, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.parseval}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p055-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p055-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p055-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p056-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p056-b003
}
\difficulty{4}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_noiseOp_sq_one_bit}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^1\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function of arity one, and let $\rho$ be any
real number. Define $T_\rho$ by multiplying the Fourier coefficient at each subset
$S$ of the coordinate set by $\rho^{|S|}$; then its expected square under the uniform
measure is
\[
  \E\big[(T_\rho f)^2\big] \;=\; \hat f(\emptyset)^2 \;+\; \rho^2\,\hat f(\{0\})^2,
\]
where $\emptyset$ and $\{0\}$ are the only two frequencies for a single coordinate. For
$d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is
$T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where
$\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform
measure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Expected $p$-th power of $|f|$ on one bit]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_abs_rpow_one_bit}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.boolCube1_ne, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.boolCube1_univ, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_bit_val_false, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_bit_val_true, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{3}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_abs_rpow_one_bit}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^1\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function of one bit and let $p\in\bbr$.
Writing $\hat f(\emptyset)$ and $\hat f(\{0\})$ for its two Fourier--Walsh coefficients,
the expectation of $|f|^p$ under the uniform measure is
\[
\E\big[\,|f|^p\,\big] \;=\; \frac{\big|\hat f(\emptyset) + \hat f(\{0\})\big|^p +
\big|\hat f(\emptyset) - \hat f(\{0\})\big|^p}{2}.
\]
Here real powers use $0^p=0$ for $p\ne0$ and $0^0=1$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{5}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lp_norm_mono}
Let $n\ge0$ be an integer, let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a function, and let $r,s$ be
real numbers with
$1\le r\le s$. Writing $\E$ for the expectation under the uniform probability measure on
$\{0,1\}^n$, the $L^r$ norm of $f$ is bounded by its $L^s$ norm:
\[
  \big(\E\big[\,|f|^{r}\,\big]\big)^{1/r}\;\le\;\big(\E\big[\,|f|^{s}\,\big]\big)^{1/s}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Two-point inequality on the unit interval]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.two_point_ineq_unit}
\leanok
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p258-b003}
\difficulty{7}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.two_point_ineq_unit}
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b006,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b007,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b002
}
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p012-b003}
Let $p$ and $b$ be real numbers with $1 \le p \le 2$ and $0 \le b \le 1$. Then the
following inequality holds:
\[
  \big(1 + (p-1)b^2\big)^{p/2} \le \frac{(1+b)^p + (1-b)^p}{2}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Two-point inequality in the case $a=0$]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.two_point_ineq_a_zero}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.two_point_ineq_a_zero}
For every real number $p$ with $1 \le p \le 2$, one has $(p-1)^{p/2} \le 1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A rearrangement inequality for a weighted square sum]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noise_l2_abs_mono}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noise_l2_abs_mono}
Let $a, b, \rho$ be real numbers with $0 \le \rho \le 1$. Then
\[
a^2 + \rho^2 b^2 \;\le\; \left(\frac{|a+b| + |a-b|}{2}\right)^{\!2} + \rho^2
\left(\frac{|a+b| - |a-b|}{2}\right)^{\!2}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[The two-point inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.two_point_ineq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.two_point_ineq_unit}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p258-b003}
\difficulty{6}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.two_point_ineq}
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b006,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b007,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b002
}
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p012-b002,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p012-b003
}
Let $a, b \in \bbr$, let $1 \le p \le 2$, and let $\rho \ge 0$ satisfy $\rho^2 \le p -
1$. Then
\[
  \big(a^2 + \rho^2 b^2\big)^{1/2} \le \left(\frac{|a+b|^p + |a-b|^p}{2}\right)^{1/p}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second norm controlled by a lower norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_bit_p2_hypercontractivity}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_abs_rpow_one_bit, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_noiseOp_sq_one_bit, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.two_point_ineq, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p116-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p259-b006
}
\difficulty{4}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_bit_p2_hypercontractivity}
\statementsource{boolean-ch10-advanced-hypercontractivity}{
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b006,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p004-b007,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b001,
  pdf-9d1751394783-p005-b002
}
\statementsource{boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}{
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p012-b002,
  pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p012-b003
}
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^1\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function on a single bit, and let $p$ be a
real number with $1\le p\le 2$. Suppose $\rho\ge 0$ satisfies $\rho^2\le p-1$. Writing
$T_\rho$ for the noise operator and $\E$ for expectation under the uniform measure on
$\{0,1\}^1$,
\[
  \big(\E\big[(T_\rho f)^2\big]\big)^{1/2}\;\le\;\big(\E\big[|f|^p\big]\big)^{1/p}.
\] For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise
operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where
$\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform
measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Signum times argument equals absolute value]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sign_mul_self}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sign_mul_self}
For every real number $x$, the product of its sign and itself equals its absolute value:
$\operatorname{sign}(x)\cdot x = \abs{x}$, where $\operatorname{sign}(x)$ is $1$ if
$x>0$, $-1$ if $x<0$, and $0$ if $x=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Absolute value of the sign of a nonzero real]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.abs_sign_eq_one}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.abs_sign_eq_one}
For every nonzero real number $x$, the sign function $\operatorname{sign}(x)$, equal to
$+1$ when $x > 0$ and $-1$ when $x < 0$, satisfies $\abs{\operatorname{sign}(x)} = 1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Cauchy–Schwarz for the Boolean inner product]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cauchy_schwarz_bool}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{4}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cauchy_schwarz_bool}
Let $n\ge0$ be an integer, let $f, g : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be functions, and write
$\E[h] = 2^{-n}\sum_{x
\in \{0,1\}^n} h(x)$ for the expectation under the uniform measure and $\langle f,
g\rangle = \E[f\cdot g]$ for the $L^2$ inner product. Then
\[
  \langle f, g\rangle \;\le\; \big(\E[f^2]\big)^{1/2}\,\big(\E[g^2]\big)^{1/2}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Sharpness of Hölder's inequality on the hypercube]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.holder_sharpness}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.expect_eq_fintypeExpect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct}
\difficulty{6}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.holder_sharpness}
Fix an integer dimension $n\ge0$ and real Hölder conjugate exponents $p, q$ (so $p, q >
1$ and $\tfrac1p +
\tfrac1q = 1$). For a function $g : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ write $\norm{g}_r =
\bigl(\E\bigl[\,|g|^r\,\bigr]\bigr)^{1/r}$ for its $L^r$ norm under the uniform measure
on $\{0,1\}^n$. Then for every function $u : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ there exists a function
$f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ with $\norm{f}_p \le 1$ and $\norm{u}_q \le \langle f,
u\rangle$, where $\langle f, u\rangle = \E[f\cdot u]$.
\end{lemma}

  {BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.holder_sharpness}
  {direct}

  {pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p013-b003}
Let $p,p'>1$ be real Hölder conjugate exponents, so that $1/p + 1/p' = 1$.
Write $\E$ for uniform expectation on $\{0,1\}^1$ and $T_{\sqrt{p-1}}$ for the
Fourier multiplier that sends the coefficient at a coordinate subset $S$ to
$(\sqrt{p-1})^{|S|}$ times that coefficient. Suppose that
\[
\E\!\left[\,\bigl|T_{\sqrt{p-1}} f\bigr|^{2}\,\right]^{1/2} \;\le\;
\E\!\left[\,|f|^{p}\,\right]^{1/p}
\]
holds for every one-bit Boolean function $f$. Then for every one-bit Boolean function
$g$,
\[
\E\!\left[\,\bigl|T_{\sqrt{p-1}} g\bigr|^{p'}\,\right]^{1/p'} \;\le\;
\E\!\left[\,|g|^{2}\,\right]^{1/2}.
\] For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise
operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where
$\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform
measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Higher one-bit norms controlled by second norm]

  {BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noise_operator_duality}
  {direct}
  {boolean-ch09-hypercontractivity-kkl}
  {pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p013-b002,
    pdf-4ba63c9394e5-p013-b001}
Fix a real exponent $q \ge 2$, and let $g : \{0,1\}^1 \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function of
arity one. Write $\norm{h}_p = \left(\E\,|h|^{p}\right)^{1/p}$ for the $L^p$ norm taken
with respect to the uniform measure, and let $T_\rho$ denote the noise operator. Then,
with noise parameter $\rho = 1/\sqrt{q-1}$,
\[
  \norm{T_{1/\sqrt{q-1}}\, g}_q \;\le\; \norm{g}_2 .
\] For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise
operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where
$\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform
measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Two-point power inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.two_point_rpow_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_abs_rpow_one_bit, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_bit_2q_hypercontractivity, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_bit_val_false, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_bit_val_true, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp_fourier}
\difficulty{5}
For every $q\in\bbr$ with $2\le q$ and all $a,t\in\bbr$,
\[\frac{|a+t|^q+|a-t|^q}{2}\le\bigl(a^2+(q-1)t^2\bigr)^{q/2}.\]
\end{theorem}
